![](/content/exams/anzca/2019/A/9/standard-image41.png){fig-alt="Alveolar-to-inspired ratios during wash-in of nitrous oxide, desflurane, sevoflurane, isoflurane and halothane"}

Inhalational Agent wash in curves graph the ratio of the Fraction Alveolar (as a surrogate of arterial partial pressure)  / Fraction Inspired volatile agent.

The rate of uptake (FA) is primarily due to the blood:gas partition coefficient. Lower B:G PC reflects lower solubility in blood so the increased partial pressure the agent exhibits.

BGPC for Desflurane is 0.42\> Nitrous Oxide 0.47 \> Sevoflurane 0.69

In terms of potency N20\<Des\<Sevoflurane, ↓potency → ↑Fi safely delivered → ↑Rate of wash in 

Nitrous oxide has a more rapid wash in rate as demonstrated on the graph due to its low potency requiring high concentrations to be delivered. 

In addition N20 Will cause a concentration effect -  as N2O is 20x more soluble then N2 the rate of uptake of N20 is greater than N2 output causing more agent to be drawn into the Alveolus  

Effect of Doubling Alveolar ventilation:

Increased alveolar ventilation increases *F*i, as it replenishes agent that has been taken up into the vasculature. the rate of volatile agent delivery to the alveolus 

→ ↑ rate of FA/FI ratio / wash in rise

Effect of doubling CO  

Increasing cardiac output increases the total drug uptake into the blood and distribution to tissues (including CNS)  but decreases the concentration/partial pressure in the blood.  This results in a slower rate of FA/FI rise.
